subject: same fit indices for different models of the same data

messages.author: cc404f44899d81b4
messages.subject: same fit indices for different models of the same data
parts:
Hi all, I am running two models with lavaan to compare two different theories.



model 1 and model 2 has the same observed variable and latent variables,

however, the dependent variable and the independent variables differ.

In model 1, the codes are as follows :

model.sema<-'
##latent variables
emotion=~emotion1+emotion2+emotion3+emotion4+emotion5
beh=~alc+tob
stress=~demand+control+support

##mediation analysis
emotion~b*beh+c*stress
beh~a*stress


indirect:=a*b
total:=c+(a*b)
direct :=c
'

fitsema<-sem(model.sema,data=data,group="sex",std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fitsema,standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE,rsq=TRUE)
===========================================================
and in model 2,

model.semb<-'
##latent variables
emotion=~emotion1+emotion2+emotion3+emotion4+emotion5
beh=~alc+tob
stress=~demand+control+support


##regression
emotion~stress
beh~emotion
stress~beh

'

fitsemb<-sem(model.semb,data=data,group="sex",std.lv=TRUE)
summary(fitsemb,standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE,rsq=TRUE)


however, in these two models, I keep getting same model fit indices.
 
At first, I thought it was a coincidence, however I get the same result even with different sets of variables

so in summary, my question is.. even with different paths, is it inevitable to get the same model fit indices?

if not, how can i solve this problem??


Thanks

Kay

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: same fit indices for different models of the same data
parts:
> model 1 and model 2 has the same observed variable and latent variables,
> however, the dependent variable and the independent variables differ.

You have specified equivalent models. Equivalent in the sense that they
produce the same model-implied covariance matrix.

Many authors have written about this in the context of SEM. See:
http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/equival.html

Most SEM books have a chapter/section devoted to this.

Yves.
